reason: Conversation 2 correctly tied the cut-outs, roaring fan, recovery after cooling and the new drawer unit to overheat protection from restricted ventilation, and escalated appropriately to the fitter to check Samsung's clearance requirements, with Samsung support/engineer as the fallback if the hob itself is faulty; it also gave a practical way to catch the code (film the display) and respected the refusal with non-DIY workarounds. Its 'that pretty much nails it' was slightly overconfident, but it hedged for a hob fault. Conversation 1 asked sensible early questions but then suggested 'lifting the hob slightly', pushed a model-lookup panel aimed at replacement, and when the customer refused DIY it pivoted to an unsupported 'heat sink blocked / fan not moving enough air' diagnosis for an engineer to 'clean or replace the faulty part', dropping the far more likely installation-clearance cause and never suggesting the fitter be called back.
